terms.definition: The straight-line change from an initial position to a final position.
terms.function: Reduces a whole journey to one net arrow that carries both a size and a direction.
terms.whereItIs: The orange arrow drawn between the start and target dots on the grid.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the quantity that velocity is built from, and it can be zero even after a long trip.

terms.definition: A quantity with both a magnitude (size) and a direction.
terms.whyItMatters: Direction is part of the information — 2 m forward and 2 m backward are not the same vector.
terms.whereItIs: Every arrow in the model, drawn with a head to show its direction.

terms.definition: The case where the final position equals the initial position, so the net arrow has no length.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the classic proof that distance and displacement are different ideas.
terms.whereItIs: Shown as a overlap badge when the target dot sits on the start dot.

terms.definition: A way of adding vectors by placing the tail of each next arrow on the head of the previous one.
terms.whyItMatters: It turns many journey legs into a single net arrow the model can compare with a direct route.
terms.whereItIs: The ghosted leg arrows that tips line up on the grid before merging.
